newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan to launch new wagon model in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Nissan to launch new wagon model in Europe.

text.p: Major Japanese car maker Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it was planning to produce a a new model of estate car in Britain designed to meet demands of European customers.
Nissan said the new estate car, a version of the Primera wagon, would be launched in summer 1998 and manufactured by its British unit.

Nissan also said that its British unit will adopt an engine made by the Peugeot SA group of companies for its Micra mini car -- its first purchase of a key auto component from a European vehicle maker.
Nissan Motor Manufacturing (UK) Ltd has plants in Sunderland, northeast England, and now produces Primera sedans and hatchback models as well as Micra mini cars.
Nissan said in a statement that it would be investing 70 million pounds ($109.55 million) in Britain for the design, development and manufacture of the new Primera wagon.
"This announcement confirms the growing responsibility of Nissan's Sunderland plants for European passenger car production," Nissan's British unit said in a statement.
Nissan said it forecast output of the new Primera would be 20,000 a year, almost double the European sales of the existing Primeras.
Nissan also said that the same British unit will adopt a 1.5-liter diesel engine made by the Peugeot SA group of companies for the Micra model.
The engine will be procured along with other parts from Peugeot Citroen Moteurs, Nissan said in a statement.
Nissan cars fitted with a Peugeot diesel engine are also scheduled to go on sale in the summer of 1998.

"Compared with Japan, demand is much stronger in the European passenger car market for diesel-engine vehicles and there have been calls for the introduction of Micra models powered by a diesel engine," Nissan said.
Currently, Micras sold in the European market have gasoline engines.

The move marks the first time for Nissan to purchase major components like engines and transmissions from a European vehicle maker, and also the first application of Peugeot-made components in Nissan vehicles, Nissan said.

The Nissan unit currently procures parts from more than 200 European suppliers for its cars, Nissan said, adding that the value of these purchases will total some 745 million pounds ($1.17 billion) a year.
